profile.headline: Software Engineer at SpaceX
profile.summary:
Accelerating  the future of technology via Electrical and Software Engineering.
Currently: SpaceX 
Former: NASA, Lockheed Martin / Blue Origin, Northrop Grumman, Aerospace Corporation. 
Go Hokies!

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Software engineer for the Starlink / Starshield constellation, responsible for writing, testing and deploying software to a fleet of over 10,000 satellites delivering connectivity to more than 9 million users worldwide. Drive the end-to-end validation and rollout of on-orbit software changes, ensuring reliable global internet service while minimizing risk to the constellation.

In this role, have implemented full-stack software, test automation, workflows, and tooling that have saved thousands of hours of software testing time, creating a fundamental architecture for faster and more frequent software deployments to the fleet. 

Developed new data analysis tools and pipelines to monitor on-orbit constellation health, detect anomalies, and inform operational decisions, significantly improving observability and responsiveness.

Also contribute directly to on-orbit capabilities by writing flight software that runs in space, enhancing satellite performance and user experience through iterative upgrades to the in-flight software stack.

positions.title: Avionics Hardware Development Engineer II
positions.description:
In addition to previous role, I designed, built, and tested life-support electronics for Polaris Dawn, enabling the world’s first commercial spacewalk and directly contributing to keeping astronauts alive in the harsh environment of space. Served as Responsible Engineer for avionics on Crew-7, owning critical hardware performance, issue resolution, and mission readiness for a flown crewed mission. Included on-console support in mission control during key test and flight operations for both of these and many more space flights.

Acted as Responsible Engineer for Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) avionics on Dragon, covering gas sensing (O₂, CO₂, VOCs), humidity and temperature monitoring, and fire/smoke detection to ensure safe cabin conditions throughout all mission phases. 

Led design and integration of Dragon pyro drivers, valve drivers, and RTD/4–20 mA sensing electronics, delivering highly reliable, flight-critical systems for human spaceflight.

positions.title: Avionics Hardware Development Engineer
positions.description:
Responsible Engineer for the Dragon Hardware-in-the-Loop (HITL) system, leading the design, integration, and maintenance of multiple full-vehicle avionics testbeds supporting both crewed and cargo variants of the Dragon spacecraft. Drove cross-functional collaboration between avionics, software, and test teams to ensure seamless hardware-software validation and mission readiness.

Designed and delivered a suite of in-house printed circuit boards (PCBs) featuring microprocessors, PHYs, CAN, RS-422, and RTD/4-20 mA DAC/ADC interfaces—achieving multi-million-dollar cost savings across Falcon, Dragon, and Starship electronics. 

Developed and deployed firmware and embedded software for flight and test systems under aggressive timelines and iterative development cycles.

Applied deep expertise in electrical and avionics engineering, including test instrumentation (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and precision measurement tools) and low-level circuit design. Contributed to the design and implementation of advanced RF communication systems, flight displays, and related avionics hardware for Falcon, Dragon, Starship/Super Heavy, and Lunar Starship missions.

positions.title: Systems Engineer
positions.description:
Technical systems engineer and early-career leader in Advanced Programs at Lockheed Martin, with deep involvement on the winning 2024 NASA Human Landing System (HLS) spacecraft as part of the Blue Origin National Team. Drove electrical and systems engineering efforts across multiple lunar and deep space programs, including Artemis/HLS (lander, refueler, descent, and transfer vehicles), NextSTEP Phase 3 U.S. habitation module studies, NASA Tipping Point technologies (lunar ISRU and cryogenic refueling), and the SWFO-L1 space weather mission proposal.

Served as Electrical Systems Requirements and Systems Engineering Lead, shaping end-to-end electrical architectures and overseeing design, integration, and development of power and RF systems, ground communications, and data systems. Led spacecraft- and vehicle-level requirements definition, traceability, verification, and testing, while generating architecture studies, mission concepts of operations (CONOPS), and trade studies to guide program-level design decisions.

Contributed to subsystem design for flight avionics, communications and tracking, docking, and GN&C, and adjudicated more than 50 design and construction standards for high-cost, high-visibility programs. Authored key interface requirements and control documents (IRD/ICD) for Orion and Gateway, produced program plans and schedules, managed risks and opportunities, and developed equipment lists, hardware channelization schemes, mass properties, and vehicle configuration baselines for large, multi-organization teams of 100+ members.

Built and maintained system models using SysML and model-based systems engineering (MBSE) tools such as Cameo and ModelCenter, supporting complex program-level analyses and digital engineering workflows. - leveraging experience with DOORS, Confluence, JIRA, CPDM/Windchill, SharePoint, MATLAB/Simulink to deliver high-quality engineering artifacts in a highly collaborative environment.

positions.title: RF Engineering Intern
positions.description: Contributed to the preliminary design of a space-based sparse array mission concept featuring a 100+ smallsat GEO cluster as part of a sponsored senior project, focusing on performance, feasibility, and system architecture. Developed SWaP (size, weight, and power) studies, formation flying analyses using MATLAB and STK, inter-cluster satellite placement concepts, and RF link budgets to characterize mission capabilities and constraints.

positions.title: Rocksat-X Program Leader
positions.description:
Led the RockSat-X design team and the Electrical/Flight Software sub-team at Virginia Tech for three years, managing end-to-end development of multiple suborbital payloads for NASA sounding rocket missions. Designed, integrated, and launched four flight experiments, including 360-degree video, a 3D printer payload, software-defined radio (AIS/ADS-B) receivers, and a small-satellite deployment mechanism for PocketQube/ThinSat-class spacecraft.

Gained four years of hands-on experience assembling and testing spaceflight hardware, designing PCBs, and evaluating COTS components for use in the space environment. Collaborated with industry partners such as Orbital ATK and ai Solutions, coordinating technical work and reviews to deliver reliable, flight-ready payloads for suborbital missions.

positions.title: Electrical Engineering Co-op
positions.description:
Supported the winning habitat design effort for the NextSTEP Phase 2 HALO program during an internship at Northrop Grumman, contributing to configuration, crew accommodation, and systems integration concepts. Helped manufacture and deliver full-scale demonstration avionics, flight systems, and crew interfaces used to validate human factors and operational concepts.

Participated in Hardware-in-the-Loop (HITL) and Day-in-the-Life (DITL) testing at NASA Johnson Space Center’s Building 9, reviewing test setups, results, and crew interaction to refine habitat design and system behavior.

positions.title: University Program Manager & Chief Technologist
positions.description:
Led the design and manufacturing of three 1U CubeSats as part of a three-satellite cluster sponsored by NASA and the Virginia Space Grant Consortium (VSGC), overseeing mission concept, spacecraft design, and on-orbit operations planning. Managed a multidisciplinary team of more than 50 undergraduate students, coordinating satellite manufacturing, environmental testing, electrical testing, and instrument verification to deliver flight-ready hardware.

Planned both Earth-to-space and satellite-to-satellite communications for the mission, including link concepts and operations procedures. The constellation launched on April 17, 2019, and mission results and architecture were published at the 31st Annual Small Satellite Conference and 2018 AGU Fall Meeting.

company.name: NASA - National Aeronautics and Space Administration

positions.title: Avionics Engineer
positions.description:
Developed the design of SharkSat, a Northrop Grumman 3U CubeSat concept featuring integrated Amazon AWS-enabled Earth imaging capabilities, with a focus on end-to-end on-orbit data delivery and processing. Led the design of the radio communication system, including frequency selection, antenna design, and packet structure definition to enable reliable downlink and mission data throughput.

Received formal training in Agile development methods and applied those practices to aerospace project organization, sprint planning, and cross-functional collaboration within the SharkSat team.

positions.title: Undergraduate Researcher
positions.description: Developed a MATLAB-based machine learning algorithm at the Virginia Tech Smart Infrastructure Lab to identify individuals from unique foot motion signatures and enable persistent tracking through multi-room building environments. The approach leveraged signal processing and pattern recognition techniques to analyze gait dynamics captured from embedded sensors, supporting applications in smart building security and occupant monitoring. Demonstrated robust performance across diverse test scenarios, contributing to broader lab efforts in intelligent infrastructure systems and data-driven facility management.

positions.title: Intern
positions.description: Conducted research focused on characterizing how manufacturing-induced deviations from design specifications impact laser batch yield and associated reproduction costs for failing units. Analyzed error propagation through fabrication processes, quantifying yield losses and cost drivers to inform process improvements and quality control strategies. Delivered actionable insights to enhance manufacturing precision and economic viability of high-volume laser production.

publications.title: The Virginia CubeSat Constellation - CubeSat Development and Atmospheric Research at Virginia Universities
Development of a 1U CubeSat as Part of a 3x1U Constellation

organizations.name: Student Engineers' Abroad Council
organizations.description: The Student Engineers' Abroad Council (SEAC) general membership is made up of engineering students who either plan on studying or interning abroad, or who have already had an international experience they'd like to share with their peers. It exists "to promote and assist engineers in the pursuit of international experiences." Oversee scholarship awards, inviting public speakers, and event planning that reaches thousands of students on campus.
